title: Two superpowers, two systems: the Cold War divide
examples: Why was it called the Cold War?
What was the Cuban Missile Crisis?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Rivals in everything, but they never fought each other directly

explain.say: Imagine two big rivals who never actually fight each other, but compete in everything: weapons, space, sport and friends. That was the Cold War, from about 1947 to 1991. Look at the two sides on the board.

draw.text: Two superpowers, two systems: the Cold War divide

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Rivals in everything, but they never fought each other directly

explain.say: Look at the left: the USA and its allies, like Britain and West Germany. They believed in capitalism, where people and companies own businesses, and in elections between parties. They formed NATO, an alliance to defend each other. What do you think they feared most?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Rivals in everything, but they never fought each other directly

explain.say: Now the right: the Soviet Union, or USSR, and its allies in Eastern Europe. They believed in communism, where the state runs the economy, under one ruling party. They formed the Warsaw Pact. Each side thought its way was fairer. Can you see why they distrusted each other?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Rivals in everything, but they never fought each other directly

explain.say: Why cold? Both sides had nuclear weapons, so a direct war could destroy everyone. Instead, they backed proxy wars, where others do the fighting, as in Korea and Vietnam. Look at October 1962: for 13 days, missiles in Cuba brought the world to the edge. How would you have felt?

faq.a: An economic system where people and private companies own businesses and decide what to make and sell, mostly through markets. In the Cold War it went with multi-party elections in the USA and Western Europe.
asks: What did the USA believe in?

faq.a: An idea that property should be shared and social classes abolished. In practice, Soviet-style communism meant the state owned businesses and planned the economy, and one party ruled without free elections.
asks: What did the Soviet Union believe in?

faq.a: In 1948 the Soviet Union blocked roads and railways into West Berlin. For about 11 months, American, British and other planes flew in food and coal, until the blockade was lifted in May 1949.

faq.q: What was the Cuban Missile Crisis?
faq.a: In October 1962 the USA found Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba. After 13 tense days, Soviet leader Khrushchev agreed to remove them; the USA promised not to invade Cuba and secretly agreed to remove its missiles from Turkey.
asks: How close was nuclear war in 1962?

faq.q: How did the Cold War end?
faq.a: Reforms by Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, economic troubles and people's protests across Eastern Europe led to the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 and the breakup of the Soviet Union in December 1991.
asks: When did the Cold War end?

facts: NATO was founded in 1949, and the Warsaw Pact in 1955.
The Cuban Missile Crisis lasted 13 days in October 1962.
The Soviet Union was dissolved in December 1991.

quiz.say: Why was it called the Cold War?

options.show: The superpowers never fought each other directly
options.say: The superpowers never fought each other directly

quiz.why: Fear of nuclear war kept the USA and USSR from fighting each other head-on.

wrong.1: Cold describes the lack of direct fighting, not the weather.
wrong.2: It lasted over 40 years, through every season.

quiz.say: Which alliance did the USA lead?
quiz.why: NATO, founded in 1949, joined the USA, Canada and Western European countries.

wrong.1: The Warsaw Pact was the Soviet-led alliance.
wrong.2: The League of Nations ended in 1946, and the USA never joined it.
